rollups.text: Patent application timeline for Darryl’s AI-tagging video-editing device: On 2024-03-15, Darryl began exploring patent protection and planned a prior-art search; on 2024-04-10, he found three similar patents that did not include AI tagging. On 2024-05-15, he said he filed a provisional application (receipt number 12345678). On 2024-07-05, he received an office action requesting clarification about claim 3’s novelty; by 2024-07-10, he and attorney Ashlee had agreed to add examples to the claim. Darryl chose to wait until November for the non-provisional filing, with a target of 2024-11-10. Drafting with Ashlee began 2024-09-01; they reviewed a 45-page draft with 12 drawings on 2024-09-10, and drawings were verified as USPTO-compliant by 2024-09-18. On 2024-11-10, Darryl said he filed a non-provisional application with the USPTO and a PCT application with WIPO. Key elapsed intervals: 36 days from prior-art search to provisional filing; 173 days from provisional filing to stated non-provisional/PCT filing; 70 days from drafting start to filing.

Prototype testing and performance timeline for Darryl’s AI-tagging video-editing device: By 2024-04-30, Darryl reported five testing cycles and 92% accuracy; by 2024-05-01, he reported seven cycles. On 2024-07-01, he reported ten tests and 96% accuracy. On 2024-09-18, he said accuracy was 96% and aimed to complete 15 cycles and reach 98% by 2024-09-30. By 2024-10-01, he had reached 16 cycles and accuracy slightly above 98%; the exact 98.2% figure was only an assistant example, not a confirmed measurement. By 2024-11-15, he reported 20 tests and 98.5% accuracy. Elapsed time from the five-cycle milestone to the 20-test report: 199 days.

Funding and investor decisions for Darryl’s invention: On 2024-05-01, Darryl rejected an offer of $15,000 for 40% equity and expressed uncertainty about that decision on 2024-05-02. On 2024-09-12, he accepted Stephen’s offer of $25,000 for 20% equity; on 2024-09-18, he planned to have a lawyer prepare an agreement and maintain regular communication. On 2024-09-14, he rejected a separate $30,000 offer for 35% equity with restrictive terms, later concluding that preserving control was preferable. On 2024-11-20, he received $10,000 in follow-up funding from Stephen and Montserrat Media Hub. On 2024-11-21, he declined a $50,000 buyout offer, saying he believed in the invention’s long-term growth. Elapsed time from the first reported rejected equity offer to follow-up funding: 203 days.

Commercialization and distribution timeline for Darryl’s AI-tagging video-editing device: Darryl planned to pitch the device to local studios with his son Francis on 2024-06-10. He met Stephen at the Montserrat Innovation Expo on 2024-05-20; Stephen requested a demonstration by 2024-07-15, and Darryl planned to present on that date. On 2024-11-20, Montserrat Media Hub executives rated a product demo 4.7/5. On 2024-11-23, Darryl finalized a distribution contract with Caribbean Tech Distributors at a 15% royalty rate. On 2024-11-25, he had a $100,000 sales-and-licensing goal by December 2025 and was unsure whether it was realistic; an assistant calculation estimated that distributor sales of about $666,667 would produce $100,000 in royalties at 15%. Darryl had also identified 2025-02-15 as the VidTag Pro launch date and planned a soft launch targeting Caribbean media companies. Elapsed time from the planned local-studio pitch to the distribution contract: 166 days.

Darryl’s attendance at the April 5 webinar was not confirmed.

People who recur in Darryl’s invention and patent discussions: Linda, Darryl’s partner, helped proofread the patent draft on 2024-09-18 and agreed with Darryl to limit work calls after 7 PM by 2024-11-25; Francis, Darryl’s son and an engineering student at Montserrat Community College, was planned to help with a local-studio pitch on 2024-06-10 and was later delegated marketing preparation; patent attorney Ashlee advised Darryl on filing and claims and worked with him on the application; mentor Jake advised Darryl on prototype-test documentation and technical claim language; Heather, a television director, suggested exploring patenting and later received patent-process insights from Darryl; Barbara, Darryl’s friend since they met at the 1995 Montserrat Arts Festival, invited him to a jazz night on 2024-05-05 and celebrated his filing with him on 2024-11-24.

On 2024-07-12, Darryl agreed to pause patent work on Saturdays to give Linda more weekend time; Sunday work remained an open question, not a confirmed schedule. By 2024-11-25, Darryl and Linda had agreed to limit work calls after 7 PM, and Darryl said he was trying to prioritize personal relationships while preparing for the planned 2025-02-15 VidTag Pro launch.
